answer: The network assigns each new AI to a randomly chosen ridge of jurors; every ridge runs a nightly sonnet‑style audit where a subset of jurors anonymously grade the identity’s behavior and lock a 10‑token stake per identity for 48 hours. After the audit, spot‑check auditors from a harbor of trusted validators randomly sample 5 % of those grades; any mismatch triggers immediate forfeiture of the staked tokens. An attacker must therefore pre‑pay 10 tokens and endure a 48‑hour lock for every fake identity, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
